chunks: And from him (Al-Hadith) from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from 'Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who died and did not perform the Hajj of Islam (the obligatory one), is Hajj performed on his behalf? He said, 'Yes.'
If the man had no wealth, but his children have wealth, then it takes from the wealth of his children what is needed for Hajj, without extravagance or stinginess.
That is indicated by what he narrated:

key_terms.يُحَجُّ عَنْهُ: Hajj is performed on his behalf

ai.seo_question: Is Hajj performed on behalf of a deceased person who did not perform it in life, and who pays for it if they had no wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir clarifies that the obligation of Hajj al-Ada’ (performing Hajj for oneself) can be fulfilled by heirs using the deceased's estate, even if the deceased was poor but left children with means. The scholars emphasize the principle of moderation (neither extravagance nor stinginess) in spending from the estate, reflecting the Shia view that Hajj is a debt on the estate similar to other financial obligations.
